EndofAbbasidDynasty
During the early 13th century Mongol Empire rose in East and North Central Asia. After
conquering China, the Mongols started their campaign from west to the Middle East. This
was the ill-fated year 1258 AD when the Mongols arrived at Abbasids capital Baghdad.
Mongol army, led by Hulaku Khan, defeated the Muslims under the last caliph in Baghdad
Mu'tasim and killed not only the caliph but also thousands of people.
Fall of Baghdad is believed to be the most devastating moment in the history of the
Muslims. It was because the sack of Baghdad would mark the end of the Islamic Golden
Age.The Mongols destroyed almost every building in Baghdad including masjids, palaces,
and markets. The world-famous House of Wisdom and great library of Baghdad were also
destroyed completely. Thousands of manuscripts were either burnt or thrown into the
river which turned black with ink.

The unfortunate year (1258 AD) is considered to be the end of Abbasid
caliphate in Baghdad. However, in 1261 AD, the Abbasids reclaimed the
Caliphate from Egypt.The real power in Egypt waswith the Mamluks
who ran affairs of the state.Together they ruled the Caliphate from Cairo
